entry.title: Quantum error correction in near-critical toric codes
entry.summary: Quantum Error Correction in Nearly Critical Toric Codes arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies error correction for topological codes pushed toward a quantum phase transition, focusing on quantum information stored in the transverse-field toric code ground states under bit-flip and phase-flip decoherence. The authors show that stabilizer measurements act almost unitarily on undecohered ground states, and that the optimal post-measurement decoder can be implemented by Monte Carlo simulation of a constrained lattice gauge theory. Numerical results show a finite threshold close to the critical point, and for phase-flip noise the threshold is proven to be independent of the transverse field throughout the topological phase.

entry.title: Quantum Pointwise Dimension (QUPID): a method for spotting classical chaos in quantum systems
entry.summary: Quantum Pointwise Dimension (QUPID): An algorithm for identifying classical chaos in quantum dynamics arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The pointwise dimension measures the effective dimensionality of classical trajectories in phase space, with regular motion confined to a torus and chaotic motion filling an energy surface. This paper implements the measure in the quantum regime using Husimi representations of wavepackets, averaging them over long times to get a stationary phase-space density. The authors report excellent agreement with classical results for both autonomous and non-autonomous systems. They also explore obtaining the pointwise dimension from a time correlation function.

entry.title: Interpretable quantum photonic generative models
entry.summary: Interpretable Quantum Photonic Generative Models arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper proposes a physical generative model for correlated multivariate data, built on homodyne detection in photonic continuous-variable circuits. Two-mode squeezing provides correlations, local phase shifts tune their strength and sign, and an adjustable interferometer redistributes them across modes. Tested on standardized log returns of financial assets, the model reproduces rich correlation structures.

entry.title: A simple proof of when maximal entanglement is needed for local state verification and discrimination
entry.summary: Simple proof of conditions requiring maximal entanglement for local state verification and discrimination arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies when entangled resources suffice for verifying and discriminating quantum states using local (separable) measurements. Using only linear algebra, the authors give self-contained proofs of two known results: the Schmidt rank of the resource must be at least that of the state being verified, and if the ranks are equal, the resource must be maximally entangled. They then show that, among pure entangled resources of local dimension at most d, a maximally entangled state of C^d⊗C^d is necessary and sufficient for perfect local discrimination of a generic orthogonal basis, however weakly entangled the resource is.

entry.title: Universal dynamics of quantum phase transitions with fractional long-range interactions
entry.summary: Universal dynamics of quantum phase transitions with fractional long-range interactions arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies the full statistics of defects produced in a quantum phase transition within a nonintegrable long-range spin chain, the fractional Ising model. The authors use time-dependent variational-principle simulations based on matrix-product states and operators. The defect number cumulants follow power laws in driving time, with exponents that vary continuously with the fractional order. At low fractional order, defect decay is slower than the Kibble-Zurek prediction, while at intermediate order the mechanism holds.

entry.title: Effective Hamiltonians and non-Hermitian physics: compressing discarded-sector information into one boundary parameter
entry.summary: Effective Hamiltonians and non-Hermitian physics arXiv · Nov 4, 2026Every realistic quantum system couples to an environment, and including it restores a closed Hermitian description, but the Hilbert space becomes intractably large. The paper uses the Feshbach–Löwdin projection to eliminate unwanted degrees of freedom exactly, yielding an effective Hamiltonian on the relevant subspace alone. This effective Hamiltonian generically becomes non-Hermitian when the eliminated subspace contains an accessible continuum and outgoing boundary conditions are imposed. Using a particle in a box with a delta barrier at its center, the authors reduce the discarded half-well to a single boundary parameter β, rederive the result via the Green's function and Dyson equation, and relate β to a self-energy term.

entry.title: Fast simulation of spectra and transport in multi-orbital quantum impurities
entry.summary: Efficient simulations of spectra and transport for multiorbital quantum impurities arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper introduces C³L, a deterministic method combining coupled-Lindblad compact bath representations with coupled-cluster theory to compute steady states and Green's functions. It has polynomial computational cost and avoids the sign problem of quantum Monte Carlo. In a real-time multiorbital benchmark, it closely matches state-of-the-art quantum Monte Carlo while cutting computational cost by four to five orders of magnitude.

entry.title: Comment on the paper "Supervised Learning with Quantum Hamiltonian Embeddings" (arXiv:2610.26833)
entry.summary: Comment on "Supervised Learning with Quantum Hamiltonian Embeddings" (arXiv:2610.26833) arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This comment discusses how quantum Hamiltonian embeddings in arXiv:2610.26833 relate to earlier Quantum Cognition Machine Learning (QCML) work, including its prior implementation on IBM quantum hardware. It examines the novelty claims of the original paper. It also considers the computational role of encoding an entire dataset in a single ground state.

entry.title: Operational thresholds for long-range entanglement in quantum networks
entry.summary: Operational Thresholds for Long-Range Entanglement in Quantum Networks arXiv · Nov 4, 2026Quantum networks share entanglement between distant nodes by chaining short entangled links with local operations that succeed only probabilistically. The paper uses a stochastic extension of concurrence percolation on hierarchical (U,V)-flower networks to derive an exact recursion for end-to-end survival probability. For the (2,2)-flower it gives a closed-form phase boundary, and it finds a second threshold in initial link quality. The results show operational reliability and link quality can compensate each other.`

entry.title: QECert: Lean Formal Foundations for Quantum Error-Correction Theory
entry.summary: QECert: Formal Foundations for Quantum Error-Correction Theory in Lean arXiv · Nov 4, 2026QECert is a Lean library that provides reusable formal foundations for quantum error-correction theory. It connects error-correction criteria, stabilizer and CSS codes, and algebraic and homological constructions in one framework. Asymptotically good quantum LDPC codes serve as the main case study, with formalized constructions and asymptotic parameter theorems for hypergraph, balanced, and lifted products and quantum Tanner codes. The library also covers Bravyi-Poulin-Terhal bounds, constant-overhead magic state distillation, and energy barriers and storage errors for quantum memories.

entry.title: Revisiting the one clean qubit case of a semi-grand challenge
entry.summary: Reopening the one clean qubit case of a semi-grand challenge arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper addresses Scott Aaronson's question of whether a quantum computer that always remains in a separable mixed state can be simulated classically in polynomial time. Earlier work claimed an affirmative answer for the one clean qubit model. The authors present a counterexample in which a pure clean qubit controls three gates acting on a maximally mixed three-qubit register, keeping all four qubits fully separable while producing a final unitary that does not match the form required by the earlier simulation result. They also give a continuous-time implementation and identify the gap in the earlier proof.

entry.title: Whether gravity-generated entanglement can be recovered when decoherence erases it
entry.summary: Recoverability of Gravitational Entanglement under Decoherence arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper asks whether gravitationally generated entanglement that decoherence has made very small can still be recovered through strictly local quantum error correction. It analyzes Newtonian gravity with localization noise, including environmental noise and collapse-model noise from GRW, CSL, and Diósi–Penrose. For GRW and CSL noise, the authors show that local error correction can make the ratio of effective gravitational interaction strength to residual decoherence rate arbitrarily large. The Diósi–Penrose model does not show this enhancement under the bipartite protocol considered.

entry.title: Ultracold polar molecules as a platform for quantum science and technology
entry.summary: Ultracold polar molecules for quantum science and technology arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This review article explains key concepts in the use of ultracold polar molecules for quantum science. Their intrinsic electric dipole moment couples strongly to microwave fields and can produce long-range, anisotropic, and tunable dipole-dipole interactions. The paper notes that such interactions can generate entanglement and enable study of quantum many-body phenomena. It also highlights recent experiments in optical tweezers and lattices and the cooling of molecular gases to quantum degeneracy.

entry.title: Study of ergotropy activation and coherence in quantum batteries charged under dissipation
entry.summary: Ergotropy Activation and Coherence in Dissipatively Charged Quantum Batteries arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies quantum batteries charged in the presence of environmental dissipation, focusing on work extraction induced by interactions. The authors derive exact analytical expressions for total, coherent, and incoherent ergotropy for two coupled two-level systems in resonant and detuned configurations. They extend the analysis to a periodic XX spin chain of N two-level systems and find that the finite-temperature coupling threshold for ergotropy activation scales as 1/N for large N.

entry.title: Synchronization Mpemba effect: a less synchronized start overtakes a more synchronized one
entry.summary: Synchronization Mpemba Effect arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper introduces the synchronization Mpemba effect, in which an initially less synchronized state overtakes a more synchronized one. It is demonstrated in dissipatively coupled quantum van der Pol oscillators, where a graph-Laplacian framework explains the mechanism as competition between a slowly decaying collective background and a fast transverse transient. The decomposition extends to networks, yielding closed-form crossing times set by eigenvalue separations and initial mode weights.

entry.title: Calculating graphene and nanoribbon band structures with quantum algorithms, judged by wavefunction quality
entry.summary: Band structure of two-dimensional graphene and of one-dimensional nanoribbons via variational quantum algorithms: from energies to wavefunction quality arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper computes the band structure of two-dimensional graphene and zigzag and armchair nanoribbons within the p_z tight-binding approximation, using one variational quantum workflow. The ground band is obtained with the Variational Quantum Eigensolver and excited subbands with Variational Quantum Deflation. Ideal simulations match exact diagonalization closely, while runs on IBM quantum hardware show energy deviations of a few hundredths of the hopping parameter. The authors also propose a wavefunction-level diagnostic based on subspace containment.

entry.title: Improved Code Rate and Distance for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Gates
entry.summary: Substantially Improved Rate and Distance for Addressable Transversal Phase Gates arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies quantum error-correcting codes that allow fully addressable transversal phase gates, a key ingredient for fault-tolerant quantum computation. Using a cyclic encoding beyond the binary CSS framework, the authors substantially improve lower bounds on rate and relative distance at every fixed Clifford hierarchy level h≥3. They present a deterministic polynomial-time algebraic-geometric construction and an exponential-time counting construction with exact verification, the latter improving the bound by roughly 2.86 times. The paper also gives an upper bound for such codes and constructs examples with 48 and 90 physical qubits supporting transversal T gates.

entry.title: A General Lorentz Framework for Tunable Semiconductor Quantum Plasmonics
entry.summary: Generalized Lorentz Framework for Active Semiconductor Quantum Surface Plasmonics arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents a generalized Lorentz framework for quantum surface plasmons in nanostructured semiconductors with arbitrary energy-momentum dispersion. The framework handles carrier nonlocality, surface carrier accumulation and depletion, and nonlocal damping. The authors also perform a quasinormal-mode analysis and demonstrate electrically controlled deep-nanoscale carrier accumulation and depletion in a semiconductor nanoantenna, which modulates its plasmonic response.

entry.title: Transferable Lindblad Variational Ansatz for Faster Steady-State Preparation
entry.summary: Transferable Lindblad Variational Ansatz for Accelerated Steady-State Preparation arXiv · Nov 3, 2026Open quantum systems naturally relax toward steady states, which underpin many nonequilibrium phenomena and quantum technologies. The paper separately controls the coherent and dissipative parts of a Lindblad generator to build a variational product formula, the Lindblad variational ansatz (LVA), which prepares steady states faster than natural relaxation. The method learns on small systems, extends to greater depth, and transfers to larger systems, with optional reference-free post-training on quantum simulators. On a bulk-dissipative Ising chain and a boundary-driven Heisenberg chain, transferred protocols reach comparable accuracy with fewer generator blocks than time-optimized first- and second-order Trotter formulas.

entry.title: Fast checking of fault-tolerant magic-state circuits built from CNOT and T gates
entry.summary: Fast verification of fault tolerant magic state preparation circuits with the CNOT + T gate set arXiv · Nov 3, 2026Magic state preparation is often one of the most expensive steps in fault-tolerant quantum computing, and checking its fault tolerance is hard. This paper proposes using the CNOT + T gate set to prepare a large class of magic states and studies how Pauli faults propagate through such circuits. The authors present Comb, a library that verifies distance-three and distance-five preparation circuits in minutes on a laptop, and use it to find a new distance-five circuit. Comparisons with circuit-level noisy simulations are used to confirm Comb's correctness.

entry.title: Quantum sensing of weak signals using two cascaded quantum van der Pol oscillators
entry.summary: Quantum sensing of a weak drive signal in cascaded quantum van der Pol oscillators arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper builds a quantum sensing system made of two quantum van der Pol oscillators linked by a non-reciprocal coupling that combines coherent and dissipative interactions. A weak signal is applied to a probe oscillator and transferred to a second, easier-to-measure oscillator, which reveals the signal's driving strength. The authors report that under certain conditions the measurement precision can reach the Heisenberg limit, and that in the strong incoherent driving regime the precision gain of non-reciprocal over reciprocal coupling grows without bound as the measurement system's two-particle loss rate approaches zero.

entry.title: Conditional Quantum Priors for Chaotic Fluid Dynamics: learning fluid-flow statistics across parameter values
entry.summary: Conditional Quantum Priors for Chaotic Fluid Dynamics arXiv · Nov 3, 2026Neural networks that predict chaotic fluid dynamics can match short-term behavior but often misrepresent long-term statistics. This paper learns a conditional quantum prior with quantum generative models that approximates selected statistics at unseen parameter values within the training range, without retraining. On Lorenz-63 it lowers mean Jensen-Shannon divergence by 56.9% compared with a classical multilayer perceptron of similar size. The prior is also used to regularize classical networks, with reported improvements on Kolmogorov flow forecasts.

entry.title: Autonomous cooling of Kerr-cat qubits extends bit-flip times to minutes
entry.summary: Autonomous cooling of Kerr-cat qubits to minutes-long bit-flip times arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies Kerr-cat qubits built from superconducting oscillators, whose bit-flip times are normally limited by excitations causing interwell switching. The authors show that the nonlinear interaction that confines the states can also cool these excitations by transferring them to a lossy readout mode. This raises bit-flip times to 450 seconds while retaining fast coherent control.

entry.title: Rotating 2D Bose-Einstein condensates in power-law traps: collapse and scaling
entry.summary: Rotating two-dimensional Bose--Einstein condensates in power-law traps: collapse, Thomas--Fermi scaling, and the inverse-square endpoint arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies two-dimensional Bose-Einstein condensates in power-law traps V=r^s/s (-2≤s≤4, s≠0), with attractive and repulsive interactions, with and without rotation. It combines scaling bounds, radial solutions, Bogoliubov spectra and imaginary-time numerical states. For attraction, the cloud collapses at the Townes coupling, with width scaling as a power of the distance from that coupling; for repulsion, it spreads to a Thomas-Fermi radius. For s=-2, the energy is exactly covariant with the cutoff length, and the condensate falls to the center for both signs of the coupling.

entry.title: Removing small energy gaps in quantum annealing by building catalysts step by step
entry.summary: Mitigating small gaps in quantum annealing through recursive XX-catalyst construction arXiv · Nov 3, 2026Adding XX-type catalyst terms to quantum annealing can widen the energy gap and speed up finding optimal solutions, but where these terms should go depends heavily on the problem. This paper proposes an iterative method that uses measurements from successive annealing runs to escape local optima and remove perturbative crossings, a common bottleneck. The approach performs consistently on scalable toy instances with up to 39 spins. On 18-spin maximum-weight independent set problems, it significantly outperforms both catalyst-free annealing and catalysts with randomly chosen XX terms.

entry.title: Edge and bulk states in Fibonacci Bose-Hubbard chains
entry.summary: Bulk and edge states in Fibonacci-Bose-Hubbard clusters arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper studies one- and two-boson energy subspaces of finite open Bose-Hubbard chains with Fibonacci-modulated hopping and zero on-site potential. For single excitations it finds two families of length-invariant states localized at the left boundary. For two bosons it reports doublon and separated-pair Tamm/Shockley edge states near either end. The authors state that second-order perturbation theory describes the spectrum and doublon edge states well in the strong-coupling regime, and suggest the results are relevant to near-term Josephson quantum simulators.

entry.title: Stretching single-photon pulses in time by intra-cavity frequency conversion
entry.summary: Temporal stretching of single-photon pulses by intra-cavity frequency conversion arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper proposes a free-space cavity with an embedded nonlinear crystal that uses frequency conversion to couple photons into a cavity mode, producing a longer pulse at a different wavelength. The authors show that the degree of stretching is strictly limited by the cavity's finesse and length. Including realistic internal losses, they report that stretching by at least two orders of magnitude is possible with high efficiency.

entry.title: Nonlinearity Suppresses Dissipation in Bath-Coupled Floquet Topological Insulators
entry.summary: Nonlinearity-Induced Suppression of Dissipation in Bath-Coupled Floquet Topological Insulators arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper studies a laser-written Floquet topological insulator periodically coupled to a photonic bath, where edge-state energy dissipation is examined. Moderate nonlinearity increases dissipation through mode mixing. Increasing the nonlinear strength to an optimal value forms highly localized traveling edge solitons that dramatically suppress dissipation.

entry.title: Bayesian-optimized magnetic field gradient detection using spin-orbit coupled Bose-Einstein condensates
entry.summary: Bayesian optimization enhanced magnetic field gradient detection based on spin-orbit coupled Bose-Einstein condensates arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes a method for detecting magnetic field gradients by linking the rotational deflection angle of a spin-orbit-coupled Bose-Einstein condensate to the gradient. The authors study how the scheme depends on its parameters and use a Bayesian optimization algorithm to search for the best combination of key parameters. The optimized gradiometer improves measurement sensitivity by a factor of five.

entry.title: Real-time analysis of the Yukawa-SYK model in closed and open systems
entry.summary: Closed- and open-system characterization of the Yukawa-SYK model in real time arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies the Yukawa-SYK model, in which bosons and fermions interact through random all-to-all couplings that drive the boson to criticality without fine tuning. Using the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism, the authors treat closed and open systems in one framework and map phase diagrams for thermal steady states, including newly identified high-temperature regimes. They also introduce markers built from two-point functions that are accessible in linear response and require no fit of conformal exponents, along with quantum Fisher information bounds.

entry.title: Simulating Electronic Structure with Qubit-Efficient Quantum DFT on a Photonic Chip
entry.summary: Quantum Simulation of Electronic Structure using Quantum Density Functional Theory on a Programmable Integrated Photonic Circuit arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents a Quantum Density Functional Theory (Q-DFT) algorithm that needs only O(log2(N)) qubits to simulate a system of N orbitals, and validates it experimentally. The authors solve the Kohn-Sham problem for the lithium hydride (LiH) molecule using an ensemble variational quantum eigensolver that targets the ground and first excited states. The experiment runs on a photonic platform combining a deterministic quantum dot single-photon source with a programmable integrated photonic circuit.

entry.title: Limits of the linearized dispersion approximation in waveguide QED
entry.summary: Breakdown of Linearized Dispersion in Waveguide QED arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies giant atoms coupled to a semi-infinite waveguide to assess when the linearized dispersion approximation holds in strong-coupling waveguide quantum electrodynamics. The authors find that atomic decoherence follows dynamics set by the numbers of bound states in and out of the continuum in the total atom-photon energy spectrum. The approximation preserves some bound states in the continuum but erases bound states out of the continuum, so its dominant role in atomic dynamics breaks down.

entry.title: Joint suppression of two-particle excitation by Kerr nonlinearity and cavity loss in a driven Holstein-Tavis-Cummings system
entry.summary: Cooperative Suppression of Two-Particle Excitation by Kerr Nonlinearity and Cavity Loss ion a Driven Holstein-Tavis-Cumming System arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper uses the numerically accurate multiple Davydov Ansatz method to study nonequilibrium dynamics in an open molecular cavity system modeled by an extended driven-dissipative Holstein-Tavis-Cummings model with Kerr nonlinearity. The authors show that Kerr nonlinearity combined with exciton-phonon coupling creates an anharmonic level structure that isolates the one-excitation manifold, producing a photon blockade regime. Cavity mode decay works together with the Kerr nonlinearity to reinforce this blockade, offering a theoretical guide for designing single-photon sources in open molecular cavity platforms.

entry.title: An exploration of spectral problems on Grassmannians
entry.summary: An Excursion into Grassmannian Spectra arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper revisits the classical spectral problem for Laplace-Beltrami and Laplace-Bochner operators on complex Grassmannians. It reviews the standard non-commutative harmonic analysis approach and then develops two complementary methods derived from quantizing the corresponding one-dimensional sigma model, with and without a magnetic monopole field. The aim is a more explicit picture of Grassmannian spectral geometry and a clearer link between harmonics, Young diagrams, magnetic bundles, and Laplacian spectra.

entry.title: Adaptive Self-Optimization of Polarization Efficiency for Low-Power NV Center Thermometers Using PAS-Q
entry.summary: Adaptive Self-Optimization of Polarization Efficiency for Low-Power NV Center Thermometers Based on PAS-Q arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper addresses the problem that high-power laser excitation of diamond nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center thermometers causes heating and reduces measurement accuracy. It proposes a reinforcement learning approach that optimizes spin polarization under low-heating constraints, combining a five-level optical pumping model with a temperature-rise constraint model built from pulsed ODMR measurements. The Progressive Action-Space Q-learning (PAS-Q) algorithm searches for optimal laser power and pulse-width combinations, and the strategy was tested in hardware. The authors report a 44% reduction in laser-induced heating, a 33% increase in spin polarization rate, and a 71% reduction in optimization time, and suggest the method may extend to other heat-sensitive quantum spin sensors.

entry.title: A paper on random purifications of isometries and quantum channels
entry.summary: On Random Purifications of Isometries and Channels arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper studies how queries to an isometry or quantum channel can be converted into queries to a random unitary completion or a random isometry dilation. It gives an efficient simulator for sequential forward queries to a fixed Haar random unitary completion. It also shows that approximating the quantum switch to constant error below 1/2 requires exponentially many channel queries.

entry.title: Time-invariant entanglement and persistent bound entanglement in a qutrit pair under collective dephasing
entry.summary: Time-invariant negativity and persistent bound entanglement in a cyclic two-qutrit family arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies how entanglement between two three-level quantum systems (qutrits) evolves under collective dephasing, a type of noise that disturbs quantum states. The states considered mix a maximally entangled state with three changing two-term states. The authors derive exact regions where the states are separable or have positive partial transpose, and give a closed-form formula for negativity. Entanglement stays constant over time when the weight of the maximally entangled state exceeds a threshold; for smaller weights it vanishes at a finite time, and in some cases remains as bound entanglement.](https://example.invalid)

entry.title: Phase-space fingerprints of collective excitations in mirror-terminated waveguide QED
entry.summary: Wigner-Function Fingerprints of Collective Excitations in Mirror-Terminated Waveguide QED arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper studies emission from singly excited collective states in a mirror-terminated waveguide quantum electrodynamics system and proposes a matched-mode witnessing protocol. The amplitudes and relative phases of the initial collective excitation are encoded in the temporal mode of the emitted single photon, enabling state verification through the common waveguide output. For a matched initial state, the selected mode contains the emitted photon, whose Wigner function shows a pronounced non-classical negative dip that serves as a fingerprint of the target state.

entry.title: Decoy-state quantum key distribution with a leaky Mach-Zehnder receiver
entry.summary: Decoy-state quantum key distribution with a leaky Mach-Zehnder receiver arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proves the security of phase-encoded decoy-state BB84 quantum key distribution using a Mach-Zehnder receiver with imbalanced beam splitters and two threshold detectors that leak fine-grained detection information. The authors derive a lower bound on Bob's single-photon contributions and combine it with the decoy-state method and a recent phase-error framework for leaky receivers. The leakage-induced correction to the phase-error rate does not depend on channel loss, giving a loss-tolerant treatment of receiver leakage even when the beam splitters are imbalanced.

entry.title: Simplified atomic Huygens' surfaces for controlling light wavefronts
entry.summary: Wavefront engineering with atomic Huygens' surfaces made simple arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes a simple bilayer square lattice of atoms with two atoms per unit cell that achieves near-unity reflectionless transmission and full 2π phase control of transmitted light, forming a near-ideal atomic Huygens' surface. Nonlocal radiative excitations provide both an even-parity electric-dipole response and an odd-parity radiation channel. A two-mode model is derived that matches full coupled-dipole simulations near optimal lattice spacings. The authors also note the platform may connect to subradiance-protected single-photon storage.

entry.title: Review of long-lived quantum memories using rare-earth ions in crystals
entry.summary: Long-lived quantum memories with rare-earth ions doped in crystals arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This review examines the physical mechanisms behind long-lived spin coherence in rare-earth-ion-doped crystals, with emphasis on the zero-first-order-Zeeman transition and dynamical decoupling. It surveys experiments reaching hour-scale spin coherence, minute-to-hour light storage, and minute-scale single-photon-level quantum storage. The paper also discusses remaining challenges for practical long-lived quantum memories and their prospects in quantum networks.

entry.title: Decoherence of an Atom's Internal State from Quantum Field Fluctuations: Why Full Relativity Matters
entry.summary: Motional Decoherence of the internal state of an atom by vacuum and thermal fluctuations of a quantum field: Necessity of a fully relativistic treatment arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies how a massive object, such as a neutral atom or an Unruh-DeWitt detector, moving at constant speed through a quantum field affects the coherence of its internal states. It compares a fully relativistic, covariant calculation with a non-relativistic approach that ignores relativistic principles. The authors find significant discrepancies between the two, even at low speeds. They recommend deriving the dynamics covariantly first and taking low-velocity limits only afterward.

entry.title: Symmetry-broken reference states for quantum diagonalization of iron-sulfur clusters
entry.summary: Broken-Symmetry Reference States for Sample-Based Quantum Diagonalization with Near-DMRG Accuracy arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies how the starting reference state affects the accuracy of sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD) for strongly correlated iron-sulfur clusters. The authors use a broken-symmetry unrestricted Hartree-Fock solution from antiferromagnetic initial guesses, which lowers the mean-field energy of the [Fe4S4(SCH3)4]2- cubane by about 534 mHa compared with restricted Hartree-Fock. Combined with multi-step configuration recovery, the energy lies 4.3 mHa above a finite-D DMRG reference. The authors conclude that reference-state preparation is a key driver of SQD energy accuracy.

entry.title: Universal control of free-electron sidebands using alternating light-electron interactions and free drift.
entry.summary: Universal Free-Electron-Sideband Control arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper studies controlling the longitudinal wavefunction of free electrons using alternating photon-induced near-field electron microscopy (PINEM) interactions and free drifts. The authors prove that a finite sequence of these operations can approximate any inner-product-preserving map from a finite-dimensional input subspace into the ideal electron-sideband Hilbert space to arbitrary accuracy, a protocol they call PINEMAD. Numerical results indicate that parameter optimization enables high-fidelity state preparation at finite electron energy spreads.

entry.title: Using language-model-designed circuits to cut the cost of quantum derivative pricing
entry.summary: Reducing the arithmetic cost of quantum derivative pricing with language-model circuit design arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper uses language-model-assisted circuit design to reduce reversible payoff arithmetic for a three-asset worst-of autocallable and a target accrual redemption forward (TARF). Compared with matched internal references, the factor-sum autocallable and windowed TARF circuits lower the product of Toffoli count and peak logical qubits by factors of 2.39 and 4.84. For the factor-sum circuit, the authors prove exact coherent execution of its integer specification, and a separate lattice calculation gives a numerical error-probability estimate. The resource scope excludes loading, payoff rotation and estimation.

entry.title: Approximate synthetic spectra of quantum systems linked to compact Lie groups
entry.summary: Approximate Synthetic Spectra of Quantum Systems Associated with Compact Lie Groups arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies synthetic spectra of position–momentum and angular-momentum systems, asking how noncommuting quantum observables can keep the geometry of a classical phase space. Under the hypotheses of Lin and Wang's approximately macroscopically unique (AMU) theorems, nonempty synthetic spectra yield AMU states. For sufficiently small ħ, the position–momentum spectrum fills the plane and the angular-momentum spectrum contains any prescribed ball. The authors prove that highest-weight coadjoint orbits lie in regional synthetic spectra under an explicit variance bound, and give function-space representations of SU(n), SO(n), and Sp(n) as further examples.

entry.title: A universal braiding example for Links–Gould topological quantum computation
entry.summary: An example of universal braiding in Links--Gould topological quantum computation arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper constructs a universal quantum computing encoding through braiding in Links–Gould fusion spaces associated with U_q^H(sl(2|1)), where q lies on the unit circle and is not a root of unity, using only neglectons. Under explicit positivity and arithmetic conditions, these spaces contain a 2^N-dimensional computational subspace with a positive definite Hermitian form. The authors prove that single-qubit operations are dense in U(2,1) and that arbitrary unitaries on N-qubit computational subspaces can be approximated with arbitrarily small leakage.

entry.title: Information-geometric bounds on fluctuation growth in open quantum systems
entry.summary: Information-Geometric Representation of Upper Bounds on Fluctuation Growth in Open Quantum Systems arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper extends the authors' earlier work on closed quantum systems to study how quantum fluctuations evolve and relate to quantum Fisher information and the quantum operations governing open-system dynamics. Using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, it derives an upper bound on fluctuation growth that separates contributions from state evolution and from the observable's explicit time dependence, reducing to a known result for closed systems. The authors also express the time evolution of density operator eigenvalues in terms of Kraus and Lindblad operators.

entry.title: Whether the universal parts of quantum field theory entanglement entropy depend on boundary condition choices
entry.summary: On the universality of entanglement entropy in quantum field theory arXiv · Nov 3, 2026Defining entanglement entropy in quantum field theory requires regularizing the entangling surface and choosing boundary conditions there. Focusing on topological theories, using three-dimensional Chern-Simons theory as an example, the paper shows under stated assumptions that different unitary choices change only non-universal terms, leaving the universal terms unchanged. It also shows that non-unitary boundary conditions can alter the universal terms, and extends the argument to two-dimensional conformal field theories.

entry.title: Heat-enhanced magnon-phonon resonance in the van der Waals antiferromagnet FePS3
entry.summary: Thermally enhanced magnon-phonon resonance in van der Waals antiferromagnet FePS3 arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper uses high-field Raman spectroscopy to study how magnon-phonon coupling in the van der Waals antiferromagnet FePS3 changes with temperature. It observes a clear avoided crossing between magnon and phonon modes over a wide temperature range, with coupling strength staying robust as temperature rises. Warming reduces the zero-field detuning, bringing the modes closer to resonance and enhancing their hybridization near the transition temperature.

entry.title: Negative logarithmic term at junctions in scalar multipartite entanglement
entry.summary: Negative Junction Logarithms in Scalar Multipartite Entanglement arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper studies multipartite entanglement at a three-region junction in a free real relativistic scalar vacuum in 2+1 dimensions. The authors report that genuine tripartite Rényi multi-entropy acquires a strictly negative logarithmic contribution for every integer n ≥ 3 and all nondegenerate sector angles. The sign of this logarithm is fixed by a negative Rényi prefactor, and a convergent angular spectral formula is given for its coefficient.

entry.title: Initialization-dependent fault sensitivity and force-balance plateaus in noisy quantum optimization
entry.summary: Initialization-controlled fault sensitivity and force-balance plateaus in noisy variational quantum optimization arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies deep variational circuits for a periodic Heisenberg chain under local gate depolarization noise, comparing how different initializations affect optimization. Full-width initializations reach low coherent error faster but incur a larger noise shift and need many more updates to converge under noise. Bounding the initial transverse generator amplitudes, inspired by many-body localization, keeps optimization low-fragility. The paper also introduces a fault-erasure fraction with a parameter-free exponential model and describes a high-noise force-balance plateau.

entry.title: Breaking quantum query barriers for graph collision
entry.summary: Breaking the quantum barriers for Graph Collision arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper studies the graph collision problem, which asks whether a known graph on n vertices has an edge with both endpoints marked, accessed through queries to the marking input bits. The authors give a bounded-error quantum algorithm using Õ(n^{92/139}) queries, refuting a conjectured Ω(n^{2/3}) lower bound, and refine it to Õ(n^{11/17}) queries. They also prove an Ω(√(n log n)) quantum query lower bound, which exceeds the O(√n) certificate complexity barrier of the positive adversary method.

entry.title: "Reading Why": An interpretable language model with Born-measured attention and exact word evidence, compiled to optics and qubits
entry.summary: Reading Why: Born-Measured Attention with Exact Word Evidence on Light and Qubits arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper builds a transformer in which every step is a Born measurement, with attention computed as |⟨q|k⟩|^4 normalised per row and a measured product replacing the feed-forward nonlinearity. On e-SNLI natural language inference it matches the test accuracy of a softmax transformer of the same size, and deleting the word its evidence ranks first changes the answer more often than for the softmax model. The same weights compile exactly to optoelectronic optics and qubits, and the attention part was partly run on an IBM quantum device.

entry.title: DynaMite: A method that speeds up fault-tolerant quantum programs by adjusting measurement timing
entry.summary: DynaMite: Dynamic Measurement Scheduling To Accelerate Fault-Tolerant Quantum Programs arXiv · Nov 4, 2026Fault-tolerant quantum computers spend most of their logical cycle time on qubit measurements, which take 43-86% of it. DynaMite is a lightweight real-time policy that selects the fastest measurement latency for each upcoming error-correction round, based on the remaining error budget and rounds left. Evaluations show it reduces logical cycle time by 1.69x on average (up to 2.29x) and lowers logical error rates to 0.46x of baseline on average (down to 0.13x).

entry.title: Quantum query lower bounds via classical moment matching
entry.summary: Quantum Query Lower Bounds from Classical Moment Matching arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper develops a quantum version of the classical moment matching method, which is used to prove lower bounds in property testing. It presents two incomparable quantum moment matching theorems, with lower bounds of Ω(N^{1/2-1/(2r)}) and Ω(N^{1/2-1/(2(2^r-1))}), the latter holding for smaller parameter ranges. The proofs combine a new continuous hybrid argument with the polynomial method. The theorems are applied to obtain optimal lower bounds for k-distinctness, k-star-freeness, planarity and outerplanarity testing.

entry.title: Data-Driven Ansatz Selection for Variational Quantum Circuits
entry.summary: Data informed Ansatz Selection for Variational Quantum Circuits arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper gives three rules for choosing a variational quantum circuit's structure and depth from the data and gate set alone, before any training. The rules concern when entangling gates are needed, how the rank of the quantum Fisher information matrix grows with depth, and how many state directions Pauli-Z readout can resolve. On the Madelon dataset, the prescribed classifier has 239 parameters and reaches 78.5% test accuracy without a grid search. Ablations confirm the effects the rules predict.

entry.title: Assessing Quantum Computing-Ready Pipelines for Stochastic Unit Commitment in Power Systems
entry.summary: On Revolutionizing Power Systems: Suitability of Quantum Computing-Ready Pipelines for Stochastic Unit Commitment Optimization arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper proposes a quantum computing-ready optimization pipeline for deterministic and stochastic unit commitment, combining classical, quantum-inspired, quantum annealing, and hybrid quantum-classical solvers on test systems including the IEEE 118-bus system. It introduces a QUBO reformulation and uses a divide-and-conquer strategy with Quantum Computing Monte Carlo simulation to handle 27,730 uncertainty scenarios. Results show the hybrid quantum method matches the classical baseline and cuts stochastic UC runtime from 40.76 to 14.79 hours, while pure quantum annealing is limited to small systems.

entry.title: Detecting Sleep Breathing Disorders with Quantum Recurrent Neural Networks
entry.summary: Sleep-Disordered Breathing Detection with Quantum Recurrent Neural Networks arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies using Quantum Recurrent Neural Networks to classify time-series data as apneic or normal breathing. The authors propose a variational classical-quantum architecture and compare it with classical recurrent neural networks on several real-world datasets. Both approaches perform comparably, with the quantum model doing better on the smallest dataset and slightly worse on the most complex one. The quantum model achieves competitive results with far fewer parameters and a small qubit count, and shows good generalization.

entry.title: Quantum memory design for smoother signal modeling
entry.summary: Spectral Quantum Memory for Implicit Neural Representations arXiv · Nov 3, 2026Implicit neural representations model signals as continuous functions, and their accuracy depends on how spectral capacity is allocated. This paper introduces the Spectral Quantum Memory Model (SQMM), in which successive quantum data-reuploading layers share a coherent quantum memory register so later layers can build on earlier computation. The authors show that, when memory read and write layers do not depend on the input, memory coupling creates no new primitive frequencies. SQMM outperforms compact quantum and classical INR baselines on audio and image reconstruction benchmarks.

entry.title: Hybrid quantum-classical model using Pauli correlators to reconstruct images
entry.summary: Hybrid Quantum--Classical Pauli-Correlator Architecture for Image Reconstruction arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents the Pauli-Correlator Autoencoder (PCAE), a hybrid quantum-classical model for image reconstruction. It splits images into patches, compresses each as a matrix product state, and uses a small quantum circuit to produce a few measured values, from which a classical neural network rebuilds the patch. Across six public datasets, PCAE2D reaches peak signal-to-noise ratios of 25.8 to 41.6 decibels. Five trained models also ran on real IBM quantum computers without retraining, reaching 25.90 to 31.52 decibels.

entry.title: Computational Hardness of Approximate Quantum Circuit Membership and Optimization
entry.summary: On the Hardness of Approximate Quantum Circuit Membership and Optimization arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper studies approximate membership for quantum circuits: deciding whether a given circuit lies within a distance of a fixed set of unitaries. It extends earlier results for the identity set under promise assumptions to promise-free inputs, other unitary sets such as Clifford or generalized permutation matrices, and several distance metrics. The authors show that the problem is PP-hard across wide ranges of parameters, with hardness persisting across quantum resources and metrics, which implies PP-hardness of certain circuit optimization tasks.

entry.title: A conditional quantum theorem on mixing bosonic inputs with quantum memories
entry.summary: A Conditional Quantum Kac-Bernstein Theorem arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper establishes a conditional quantum Kac-Bernstein theorem for mixing two independent, finite-mode bosonic inputs that carry quantum memories. It gives an exact criterion for when the two outputs are conditionally independent given both memories. Each input decomposes into orthogonal memory sectors that share a common Gaussian state and a bosonic memory factor, up to sector-dependent physical displacements.

entry.title: Formal reasoning about concurrent quantum circuits that share qubits
entry.summary: Reasoning about Shared-Qubit Concurrency in Quantum Computing arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents a semantic model for running quantum circuits in parallel, giving a formal basis for studying concurrency when circuits share qubits. The authors extend the classical Owicki-Gries method to quantum circuits, allowing components to be verified separately from their interference. They propose proof rules for establishing correctness of parallel quantum circuits and prove these rules are sound with respect to the model.

entry.title: Hardware-efficient reinforcement-learned scheduling for quantum LDPC decoders
entry.summary: Hardware-Efficient Reinforcement-Learned Scheduling for Quantum LDPC Decoders arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents hardware implementations of three decoders for the [[288,12,18]] bivariate bicycle quantum LDPC code: conventional belief propagation (BP), reinforcement-learned sequential BP (RL-S), and a bucket-based variant (BRL-S). BRL-S uses quantized priorities and first-in, first-out buckets to simplify scheduling instead of heap-based management. FPGA synthesis shows about 68 to 72 percent lower lookup-table usage than RL-S, and ASIC synthesis shows 63 to 67 percent lower area and 64 to 69 percent lower estimated power.

entry.title: Room-temperature optical readout of aqueous Cu(II) spin coherence via symmetry-breaking chelation
entry.summary: All-optical room-temperature spin coherence of aqueous asymmetrically chelated Cu(II) for chemoselective discrimination arXiv · Oct 18, 2026The paper addresses the difficulty of optically reading out molecular electron spins in water, where Cu(II) previously needed about 1 M concentrations. Chelating Cu(II) with EDTA breaks symmetry, boosting absorption and magnetic circular dichroism by 7.3- and 5.6-fold and enabling spin readout down to 100 μM. Histidine extends the apparent dephasing time T2* from about 0.54 ns to about 0.8 ns in a concentration-dependent way, while glycine has no measurable effect.

entry.title: Coherence of Gaussian quantum states depends on the chosen frame
entry.summary: Approximation of a continuous-variable Gaussian state by discrete-variable quantum states arXiv · Oct 5, 2026This paper describes Hilbert space coherence using a tight frame of all canonical coherent states instead of an orthonormal basis. Gaussian states are simpler to describe in this coherent-state frame than in the Hermite-Gauss basis. The authors derive an explicit formula for the frame-dependent coherence of mixed Gaussian states in terms of the covariance matrix determinant and trace. They also construct discrete-variable states that rapidly converge to each mixed Gaussian state as the Hilbert space dimension grows to 15 or more.

entry.title: Simulating exotic particle statistics on a quantum processor
entry.summary: Analog quantum simulation of paraparticle statistics arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper emulates a type of paraparticle, called R-paraparticles, which are indistinguishable particles with nonlocal internal degrees of freedom. The researchers use a superconducting qubit lattice to model paraparticles that obey a generalized Pauli exclusion principle. Measurements show a 180-degree phase shift under exchange, antibunching independent of internal states, and thermal occupation matching neither Bose-Einstein nor Fermi-Dirac statistics. The results show that parastatistics can be observed on quantum simulation platforms. ★★★★ Notable: The authors emulate R-paraparticle statistics on a superconducting qubit lattice, reporting a 180-degree exchange phase and antibunching under beamsplitter interference.

entry.title: Long-range entangled critical state caused by coherent errors
entry.summary: Long-range entangled criticality from coherent errors arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper shows that coherent errors can drive the clean surface code into an extended critical regime that is long-range entangled, with a diverging Markov length. The authors establish two general results linking topology, coherent information and mixed-state entanglement, and extend local recovery constructions to locally parameterized families. They apply these results to the honeycomb surface code and relate conditional mutual information to conductance in a Majorana network model. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report that coherent errors induce a long-range entangled critical phase in the surface code, with general results on mixed-state entanglement.

entry.title: A quantum identity authentication protocol that encodes random sequences into perturbed probability amplitudes of entangled states.
entry.summary: Quantum identity authentication protocol via perturbed probability amplitudes arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes a quantum identity authentication protocol based on perturbed probability amplitudes, aimed at establishing mutual trust between communicating parties in the post-quantum era. The protocol encodes a random sequence onto the probability amplitudes of quantum entangled states and generates n-bit random authentication information from n-bit pre-shared information. The authors state that it resists impersonation, CNOT, and entanglement measurement attacks, and can be extended to a bi-directional version.

entry.title: Anti-distinguishability of quantum channels: a study of perfectly excluding candidate channels with a single query
entry.summary: Anti-distinguishability of quantum channels arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies single-query perfect anti-distinguishability, or exclusion, tasks for finite ensembles of quantum channels, mainly using Choi operators and process POVMs. It distinguishes weak exclusion, where each outcome excludes a candidate with certainty, from strong exclusion, where every candidate must also be excluded with nonzero probability. The authors derive conditions based on the support of the Choi operators and apply them to measure-and-prepare, state-space contraction, Pauli, and replacer channels.

entry.title: Runtime compilation of quantum circuits using PQF-based Rz synthesis
entry.summary: Runtime Compilation for Quantum Circuits with PQF-Enabled R_z Synthesis arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper addresses reducing T-gate counts in fault-tolerant quantum computing with surface codes. It proposes R²-PQF, a runtime routing protocol that dynamically computes lattice-surgery paths for circuits synthesized with PQF, implemented via a wavefront breadth-first search on FPGA and ASIC. For a 300-qubit Ising Hamiltonian circuit, the median logical time-step is 1.51 µs, and the method is reported to be 1.34× faster on average than a stalling baseline, and up to 1.76× faster.

entry.title: Gaussian quantum integrated sensing and communication: a quantum scheme that communicates over an optical link while locating a defect, and studies how to split shared entanglement between the two tasks
entry.summary: Gaussian Quantum Integrated Sensing and Communication arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies a quantum integrated sensing and communication problem over an optical link, where a low-power transmitter communicates with a receiver while locating a defect that produces a backscattered signal. The system is modeled as a lossy thermal-noise bosonic channel, and two protocols are proposed that use shared Gaussian entanglement, either two-mode or three-mode squeezed vacuum states, to assist both sensing and communication. The results characterize achievable communication-rate and sensing error-exponent regions, which outperform time-sharing schemes and demonstrate a quantum advantage.

entry.title: Weyl superfluids from trivial bands via interaction in an optical Raman lattice
entry.summary: Interaction-driven Weyl superfluids from topologically trivial bands in an optical Raman lattice arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes a way to realize Weyl superfluidity in the strongly correlated regime of a three-dimensional optical Raman lattice, using pairing that arises from the interplay of large Zeeman splitting and strong Hubbard interaction. Mean-field calculations yield Weyl superfluids with two, four, or eight nodes, as well as fully gapped weak topological superfluids. Tuning interaction strength and filling drives transitions between these phases and controls the number of Weyl nodes. An experimental implementation with ultracold potassium-40 atoms is also proposed.

entry.title: Sharp entropy uncertainty bounds for discrete quantum quasiprobability distributions
entry.summary: Tight Quasiprobabilistic Entropic Uncertainty Relations for Discrete Quantum Systems arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies entropic uncertainty for quasiprobability distributions in discrete quantum systems. The authors prove that for Kirkwood-Dirac distributions built from mutually unbiased bases and for Gross-Wigner distributions, the entropy lower bound is attained by pure states with positive quasiprobability distributions. They also show that Kirkwood-Dirac distributions with large nonpositivity have large uncertainty.

entry.title: Adaptive qubit encoding for optimizing continuous variables on quantum hardware.
entry.summary: Adaptive Qubit Encoding for Continuous-Variable Quantum Optimization arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents a framework for optimizing continuous-variable functions on qubit-based quantum hardware. It combines adaptive discretization with an iterative local mapping of the objective onto an effective spin-glass Hamiltonian. The method is tested on unconstrained and constrained n-dimensional Gramacy-Lee benchmarks and on a proof-of-concept inverse-planning problem in intensity-modulated radiotherapy for cancer treatment. The results indicate the framework can produce competitive solutions.

entry.title: How internal electric fields affect precise diamond magnetometry
entry.summary: The Impact of Internal Electric Fields on Accurate Diamond Magnetometry arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper examines how random internal electric fields, caused by charged dopants in diamond, shift the spin-transition frequencies of nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers and affect magnetometry accuracy. The authors built a Monte Carlo model that reproduces the asymmetric spectral lineshapes seen in experiments and used it to quantify the resulting errors. Standard analysis shows systematic errors above the g-factor uncertainty below about 5 mT, and the proposed fitting function reduces this error by nearly an order of magnitude.

entry.title: A method for describing unitary matrices, applied to nucleon-nucleon scattering matrices above the inelastic threshold.
entry.summary: Parametrization of unitary matrices, parametrizing the symmetric S matrix and the NN S matrix above the inelastic threshold arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper notes that existing S-matrix representations used to analyze nucleon-nucleon (NN) scattering above the inelastic threshold do not simultaneously satisfy implicit unitarity, generality, and a connection to low-energy (Stapp) parameters. The author presents an S-matrix representation that meets these requirements and can be used to solve the corresponding inverse scattering problem. As a by-product, a parametrization of an n-dimensional unitary matrix is derived.

entry.title: How quantizing the pump changes optimal measurements in quantum sensing
entry.summary: Pump quantization changes optimal measurements for quantum sensing arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper examines quantum phase sensing when the pump light is treated as a quantum object rather than an undepleted classical resource, as earlier analyses assumed. It finds that quantum advantage persists after pump quantization but depends critically on the nonlinear (χ⁽²⁾) source dynamics. Heisenberg scaling is reached in the regime of strong pump depletion, where signal flux is maximized, and this requires a joint nonlinear measurement of the whole pump-signal system rather than standard photon counting.

entry.title: Effective non-Hermitian dynamics from post-selection methods
entry.summary: Non-Hermitian effective dynamics from post-selection protocols arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper shows that Feshbach projection, the Lindblad master equation, and the ancilla approach can all be unified through the Kraus map formalism, yielding non-Hermitian time evolution once an appropriate post-selection procedure is applied. It derives an exact expression for conditional system dynamics and examines the approximations of each approach and the non-Hermitian Hamiltonians they produce. The authors justify the right-right formalism for computing expectation values and conclude that traditional thermodynamic equilibrium does not apply to general non-Hermitian systems.

entry.title: Paper on unital qubit channels being 3-noisy, i.e., simulable with a three-dimensional maximally mixed environment
entry.summary: Unital qubit channels are 3-noisy arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper studies algebraic and environmental properties of mixed unitary quantum operations. It shows that the composition of two uniformly n-mixed unitary channels is again n-noisy, and that this property is invariant under unitary equivalence. Using majorization and the divisibility of Kraus rank-four unital qubit channels, the authors demonstrate that any unital qubit channel can be physically simulated with a three-dimensional maximally mixed environment.

entry.title: Kramers degeneracy in Liouvillian operators
entry.summary: Liouvillian Kramers Degeneracy arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper shows that time-reversal and parity symmetries together enforce Kramers degeneracy in Liouvillian superoperators acting on mixed states. The authors construct dissipative many-body models of interacting fermions and spins that exhibit this degeneracy. Their complex spectral statistics follow the non-Hermitian random matrix ensembles of the corresponding symplectic class.

entry.title: High-fidelity quantum gate learning with physics-informed neural networks
entry.summary: High-fidelity quantum gate learning via physics-informed neural networks arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes a physics-informed neural network (PINN) method for learning control fields that implement one- and two-qubit quantum gates, trained with the time-dependent Schrödinger equation. Unitary simulations report very low average gate infidelities for Hadamard and controlled-NOT gates under several interaction types. The authors also test the control fields under dephasing and amplitude damping, and show that boundary-adapted Chebyshev expansions can compactly represent the learned controls.

entry.title: Quantum circuit optimization that splits circuits optimally and accounts for entanglement
entry.summary: Entanglement-Aware Quantum Circuit Optimization through Globally Optimal Partitioning arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper presents a scalable framework that selects globally optimal partitions of a quantum circuit using an integer linear program, with objectives such as minimizing partition count or weighted execution cost. The selected partitions are resynthesized with an operator-Schmidt rank (OSR) based method that exploits their internal entanglement. On 772 local unitary targets, OSR produced 741 verified syntheses versus 617 for BQSKit, and matched or reduced CNOT counts in all 617 jointly verified pairs.

entry.title: Rebuilding the conformal algebra from a critical ground state on the (fuzzy) sphere
entry.summary: Reconstruction of the conformal algebra from a critical groundstate on the (fuzzy) sphere arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper builds on earlier work that reconstructs the dilatation operator (sphere Hamiltonian) from a regulated conformal field theory ground state. It develops methods to construct the full global conformal algebra and tests them using fuzzy sphere regularization. These methods outperform constructions based on a Hamiltonian density, are model-independent, need no extra tuning, and improve with system size. The authors also identify conformal primary states and provide further support for a model of short-distance corrections to the entanglement Hamiltonian.

entry.title: Optimized finite-key security for satellite uplink entangled quantum key distribution
entry.summary: Optimised finite key for satellite up-link entangled quantum key distribution arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies entanglement-based quantum key distribution from ground to satellite, using a more rigorous security analysis that accounts for finite-size effects from short block lengths. It finds that the optimal source operation changes slightly under finite statistics, with the pump power should be slightly lowered. The authors estimate annual key rates for the Heriot-Watt ground station and several satellite parameters, finding that accumulating all raw key material before extracting a secure key yields a higher annual key rate.

entry.title: A quantum banking system that uses quantum tokens to secure cash withdrawals
entry.summary: Quantum banking system for secure cash withdrawal arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper proposes a quantum-secure cash withdrawal framework that replaces reproducible classical credentials with quantum tokens for authentication. It integrates token generation, authentication, and verification into existing banking workflows using experimentally motivated quantum control techniques. According to the authors, the approach is intended to mitigate card cloning, credential theft, and counterfeiting.

entry.title: Renormalised hydrogen partition function and Saha ionisation equation
entry.summary: Renormalisation of Hydrogen Partition Function and Saha Ionisation Equation arXiv · Oct 16, 2026The paper addresses the divergence of the neutral hydrogen atom partition function that appears in the Saha ionisation equation, caused by the rapidly growing degeneracy of excited states. The authors propose a regularisation and renormalisation procedure that yields a well-defined partition function. This allows calculation of energy level populations and ionisation state of hydrogen plasma versus temperature and pressure. The results reduce to the Saha equation at low temperatures and describe deviations from it at higher temperatures, with application to the solar core and atmosphere considered.

entry.title: Entanglement Resource Allocation for Quantum Integrated Sensing and Communication
entry.summary: Entanglement Allocation for Quantum Integrated Sensing and Communication arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies how a limited pool of entanglement can support both communication and distributed sensing in future quantum networks. It proposes a network-level quantum integrated sensing and communication (Q-ISAC) framework in which a quantum base station dynamically allocates Bell pairs and partitions sensing resources among multiple GHZ probes. The authors model effective quantum Fisher information and solve the allocation problem with a hierarchical constrained proximal policy optimization (HC-PPO) method. Numerical results show that GHZ probing needs about 27 to 30 percent fewer sensing qubits than separable probing under the same sensing requirements.

entry.title: Hardware-aware design of quantum reservoir computing for insurance claims forecasting
entry.summary: Hardware-Aware Design and Layout Selection in Quantum Reservoir Computing for Insurance Claims Forecasting arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper examines whether small quantum reservoir computing models can forecast next-day motor-insurance claim counts competitively with classical models, and whether their predictions hold up on noisy hardware. A six-qubit gate-based reservoir was evaluated on 232 held-out test days, where four of five candidates did not differ significantly from ridge regression. On the IBM Kingston processor, hardware-aware qubit layouts gave lower error than Qiskit's default layouts in every paired round.

entry.title: Factorized Approximate Inverse Preconditioners for Tensor Train Solvers
entry.summary: Factorized approximate inverse preconditioners in the tensor train format arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents a preconditioning method that speeds up Tensor Train (TT) solvers for symmetric positive-definite linear systems. The authors extend the Factorized Sparse Approximate Inverse framework to tensor networks, building the preconditioner as the product of a TT operator and its transpose, which satisfies the requirements of the Conjugate Gradient method. Tests on anisotropic diffusion and Poisson problems show consistent reductions in iterations, with net speedups of up to 25% in ill-conditioned time-stepping settings. The authors also introduce the open-source Julia library DifferenTT.jl.

entry.title: Certifying particle indistinguishability in interferometers without tailored hardware
entry.summary: Marginal bunching for in situ certification of multiparticle indistinguishability arXiv · Oct 19, 2026The paper proposes a scalable, efficient in situ method to test whether identical bosons or fermions are indistinguishable in linear interferometer experiments. It applies to any generic linear interferometer. For particles in distinct input ports of a Haar-random unitary interferometer, the required number of runs scales polynomially with particle number, interferometer size, and inverse precision, with high probability. The method remains polynomial under uniform particle loss if the inverse single-particle survival probability is polynomially bounded. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose an in situ method to certify multiparticle indistinguishability in linear interferometers, exploiting quantum parallelism and bunching/anti-bunching tendencies. They report that fo

entry.title: Maximum purity of absolutely separable and PPT quantum states in qutrit-qudit systems
entry.summary: Maximum purity of absolutely separable and absolutely PPT states in qutrit--qudit systems arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This paper studies bipartite quantum states in qutrit-qudit systems C^3⊗C^n with n≥3. It determines the maximum purity of absolutely separable states and absolutely PPT states, showing both classes share the same maximum. The authors also bound the minimum partial-transpose eigenvalue reachable by global unitary transformations in terms of purity and characterize the states attaining this bound. These results confirm the inscribed-polytope purity conjecture for all qutrit-qudit systems. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show that absolutely separable and absolutely PPT qutrit-qudit states in C³⊗Cⁿ (n≥3) share the same maximum purity, confirming the inscribed-polytope conjecture of Ahiable, Kothakonda and

entry.title: Quantum hypothesis testing that can refuse to decide: exact error-exponent trade-off
entry.summary: Binary Quantum Hypothesis Testing with a Rejection Option: The Exact Error-Exponent Trade-off arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper studies binary quantum hypothesis testing on finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, where the test may reject, and the rejection probabilities under both hypotheses must vanish exponentially. It gives necessary and sufficient conditions for a quadruple of error and rejection exponents to be achievable, consisting of three single-letter conditions. Two involve Petz–Rényi quantities and match a converse bound conjectured to be tight by Ji and Regula, while the third involves α–z Rényi quantities. The proof combines a sector decomposition within Schur–Weyl blocks, an explicit one-shot measurement construction, and an exact minimax argument. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give an exact characterization of the error-exponent trade-off for binary quantum hypothesis testing with rejection, report that two conditions match the Ji-Regula conjectured tight bound,

entry.title: Quantum lower bounds for finding and testing k-to-one collisions in strings
entry.summary: Quantum Lower Bounds for Collision Problems arXiv · Nov 1, 2026The paper studies quantum query complexity for Promised k-to-one Finding on an exactly k-to-one string over a fixed alphabet. It gives tight lower bounds for both adaptive algorithms and one-round non-adaptive algorithms, the latter matching classical birthday sampling even with entangled queries. It also proves a non-adaptive lower bound for k-to-one Testing, resolving an open question from Koiran, Landes, Portier, and Yao. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors report tight adaptive and one-round non-adaptive quantum query lower bounds for promised k-to-one finding on exactly k-to-one inputs, with the one-round bound matching classical birthday s

entry.title: Full-order mutual information from modular flow, without replicas
entry.summary: Mutual information to all orders from modular flow: a replica-free approach arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper derives an all-orders long-distance expansion of vacuum mutual information between two disjoint balls in generic d-dimensional CFTs. It uses a radial sewing expansion, a modular response formula for relative entropy, and geometric modular flow, avoiding replica-number analytic continuation. In the two-dimensional Ising CFT, the first ten radial orders are computed and show good agreement with lattice data at finite separation.

entry.title: Lee-Yang theorems for q-deformed oscillators and doubly-scaled SYK
entry.summary: Lee-Yang theorems for q-deformed oscillators and doubly-scaled SYK arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper proves that the vacuum partition function of the q-deformed oscillator has all its zeros on the imaginary axis (the Lee-Yang property) for every q in [-1,1), confirming conjectures by Okuyama from 2023. Using the link between q-deformed oscillators and the doubly-scaled SYK Hamiltonian, the authors show that the annealed SYK partition function has the same property in the thermodynamic limit. They conclude that the quenched SYK partition function has a zero-free strip of constant width with high probability. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove the q-deformed oscillator partition function has Lee-Yang zeros and extend this to doubly-scaled SYK.

entry.title: Single-pass stochastic cooling for electron microscopy: a theoretical study on reducing electron beam energy spread via strong electron-light coupling in nanophotonic structures
entry.summary: Single-pass stochastic cooling for electron microscopy arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper addresses the brightness limits of electron sources in electron microscopes by proposing single-pass stochastic cooling inside the microscope, using strong electron-light coupling in nanophotonic structures. The approach is laser-free, compatible with continuous-wave operation, and aims to improve longitudinal emittance without loss. The authors develop a fully quantum mechanical model valid in the strong coupling regime and derive an analytic asymptotic formula for the optimal cooled energy spread. Numerical simulations show that reduced energy spread corresponds to higher electron quantum state purity and smaller longitudinal phase space area.

entry.title: Unifying entanglement and nonclassicality through the Narcowich-Wigner spectrum
entry.summary: Unifying entanglement and nonclassicality via the Narcowich-Wigner spectrum arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies the relationship between quantum entanglement and nonclassicality, which is known to be linked through two-mode mixing. The authors extend this connection to arbitrary multimode Gaussian evolutions. They use the Narcowich-Wigner spectrum to quantify single-mode phase-space nonclassicality and derive sufficient conditions for a single-mode state to generate NPT entanglement after a multimode Gaussian unitary evolution. These conditions tighten and generalize existing criteria.

entry.title: Quantum tomography in Schwartz space, a function-space framework for reconstructing quantum states
entry.summary: Quantum tomography on Schwartz space arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper shows that standard quantum tomography results, usually proven in Hilbert spaces, can also be established within the theory of Schwartz spaces. It shows that quantum states are equivalently characterized by their Wigner function, the characteristic function of that Wigner function, and the probability distributions of linear combinations of position and momentum. The techniques are presented in a form more accessible to physicists.

entry.title: Exceptional points and optimized encoding in qubit stabilizer codes
entry.summary: Exceptional Points and Optimized Encoding in Qubit Stabilizer Codes arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies stabilizer codes under continuous blind stabilizer measurements, casting error correction as a Liouvillian spectral problem where Hamiltonian terms compete with dissipative error channels. The authors show this competition generically produces Liouvillian exceptional points, whose occurrence at weak error rates is limited by the code distance, and that these points accelerate the decay of encoded coherences. They then optimize the logical qubit encoding using Lindblad operator eigenmodes and apply it to the [[5,1,3]] code, where it outperforms naive encoding near the exceptional point.

entry.title: Surface charges and quantum reflection of hydrogen-isotope beams at grazing incidence
entry.summary: Surface charges and quantum reflection of hydrogen-isotope beams at grazing incidence arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper theoretically studies how trapped electric charges on dielectric mirrors affect the specular reflection and diffuse scattering of hydrogen, deuterium, and tritium atoms at grazing incidence on SiO2/Si and MgF2 surfaces. The authors show that the charge distribution determines the polarization potential seen by the atoms, which changes the threshold behavior of reflection. At a surface charge density of 10^12 cm^-2, absorption increases by up to 26% for SiO2/Si and by two to three times for MgF2.

entry.title: Lossless propagation bounds for long-range fermionic interactions
entry.summary: Lossless propagation bounds for long-range fermionic interactions arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proves propagation estimates for extensive fermionic many-body interactions with polynomial time growth, no loss of spatial decay, and an optimal threshold for the polynomial spatial exponent. The authors construct local representatives of evolved interactions on metric spaces with polynomial volume growth. The threshold a > d_vol is shown to be optimal in general. The results yield dynamical estimates for perturbation theory with extensive perturbations. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors give lossless propagation bounds for fermionic interactions with polynomial growth and prove the threshold a>d_vol is optimal, with applications to gap stability and adiabatic theory.

entry.title: Faster thermalization of 1D noncommuting Hamiltonians using system-bath interactions with linearly many ancillas
entry.summary: Efficient thermalization of one-dimensional noncommuting Hamiltonians via system-bath interactions with Theta(n) ancilla qubits arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper proves rapid convergence of a system-bath algorithm that prepares Gibbs states of one-dimensional noncommuting Hamiltonians at any fixed positive temperature. For a chain of n qudits, it reaches trace-norm error ε in expected total evolution time Õ(n/ε). This improves the previously proved Õ(n^6/ε) bound for single-ancilla samplers, up to logarithmic factors. ★★★★ Notable: The authors improve the bound for single-ancilla system-bath Gibbs samplers from O(n^6) to linear system-size dependence, with theoretical analysis.

entry.title: Quartet state of the neutral nitrogen-vacancy center in diamond and optimized near-infrared spin readout
entry.summary: Quartet state of the neutral nitrogen-vacancy center in diamond and optimized spin readout under near-infrared two-photon excitation arXiv · Nov 3, 2026After photoionization, the nitrogen-vacancy center in diamond leaves a neutral defect in a metastable quartet state of unknown energy. Using tunable femtosecond two-photon optically detected magnetic resonance, the authors find the spin-contrast onset at 1.23 ± 0.02 eV and place the quartet 0.54 ± 0.04 eV above the neutral ground state. This threshold makes 1060–1075 nm the optimal excitation for spin readout, giving 26–37% higher shot-noise-limited sensitivity than 1030–1040 nm.

entry.title: Agentic Pipeline Verifying Topological Code Mapping to Quantum Hardware via Lean
